column6: summary
Branches and careers in the data and AI discipline — what the specialisms are, what each one actually does day to day, and how people move between them.

What quantum computing is and how quantum computers differ from Turing machines; the threat to current public-key cryptography; quantum-safe encryption; NIST and the CRYSTALS-Kyber algorithm; and a Java implementation using the Legion of the Bouncy Castle.

A philosophically different way of solving modern software problems — from one codebase in Dubai to a fleet of services on AWS, told through the Careem story: the monolith, the seams, decomposition, service boundaries, data ownership and the operational cost of the trade.
How programming began — the machines, the people and the ideas that turned mathematics into instructions a machine could follow.
Principles of material user interface design and UX-based design in practice — material UI guidelines, colour theory, and worked examples of UX-driven design decisions.
Why versioning matters and the ways teams get it wrong — no versioning, timestamps, build numbers — and how semantic versioning fixes the contract between a release and the people who depend on it.

What a workflow is and the stages software passes through from development to release; a comparison of the common Git workflows — centralised, feature branch, Gitflow, forking — and how to pick one for a given team.
How a traditional software house uses Agile to deliver products efficiently — people, process and a case study, with a look at the classes of software house and where Agile fits each.
The confusion matrix; the high-accuracy trap; choosing the right metric and building a balanced one; inventing your own metric when the standard ones do not fit; ROC and AUC.

Shakespeare and the monkey with a keyboard; the cost of brute force measured against the age of the universe; Darwinian natural selection as a search strategy; selection, crossover and mutation; and the Mona Lisa reconstruction.
A six-session course on the Django framework — the client and server ends of a web application, MVT, project structure, models, templates, views and forms — with a group activity and a quiz.
Designing reports in Jaspersoft Studio against a data warehouse and publishing them to Jaspersoft Server.
What a unit test is, who writes it and why; unit testing in extreme programming; JUnit annotations, assertions and naming conventions; mocking with Mockito; and test-driven development, hands on.
Institutionalising CI/CD in an engineering organisation — code stability, automated testing, version control, code quality and reviews, and automated deployment with runners.
Divide and conquer as a processing methodology; parallel processing and the scalability problem; the three Vs of big data; and the map and reduce phases in practice.
A day in your life — how many hours are there in your day, and what the answer says about how work is planned.

column2: ETL and Data Warehousing using Talend
column6: Built for KMITS at the Department of Health, Philippines — Talend design, dimensions and facts, metadata, staging tables, and the development process and protocols around them.
What R is and why it exists; the building blocks of the language; built-in functions and packages; and a deep dive into the Titanic dataset.
What the cloud is and what was new about it; why cloud; the cloud era and what it displaced; and what it takes to do it yourself.

A five-day workshop — the IDE and conventions; variables, operators and statements; functions and program control; arrays; searching and sorting; objects, classes and OOP; communication between objects; inheritance; dynamic structures; and threads. Each day ends with a practice set.
